source_text: Illi in uos saeuiant. qui nesciunt, cum quo labore uerum inueniatur et quam difficile caueantur errores; illi in uos saeuiant, qui nesciunt, quam rarum et arduum sit carnalia phantasmata piae mentis serenitate superare; illi in uos saeuiant, qui nesciunt, cum quanta difficultate sanetur oculus interioris hominis, ut possit intueri solem suum — non istum, quem colitis caelesti corpore, oculis carneis et hominum et pecorum fulgentem atque radiantem, sed illum, de quo dictum est per prophetam: ortus est mihi iustitiae sol, et de quo dictum est in euangelio: erat lumen uerum, quod inluminat omnem hominem uenientem in hunc mundum —: illi in uos saeuiant, qui nesciunt, quibus suspiriis et gemitibus fiat. ut ex quantulacumque parte possit intellegi deus; postremo illi in uos saeuiant, qui numquam tali errore decepti sunt, quali uos deceptos uident.
thought_title: Only the ignorant rage against you
orientation: Augustine is addressing the Manichaeans, explaining that those who attack them harshly do so because they do not know how hard it is to find truth, avoid error, and be healed from false imaginings.
pass_a_gloss: They against you let them rage, who do not know, with how much labor [the] truth is found and how difficultly errors are avoided; they against you let them rage, who do not know, how rare and arduous it is [the] carnal phantasms [by] [the] serenity of [a] pious mind to overcome; they against you let them rage, who do not know, with how great difficulty is healed [the] eye of [the] inner man, that it may be able to look upon its [own] sun — not that [one], which you worship [in] [a] heavenly body, [with] [the] fleshly eyes both of men and of beasts shining and radiating, but that [one], about which it was said through [the] prophet: has arisen for me [the] sun of justice, and about which it was said in the gospel: it was [the] true light, which illuminates every man coming into this world —: they against you let them rage, who do not know, with what sighs and groans it happens, that from however small [a] part God can be understood; finally they against you let them rage, who never [by] such error were deceived, as you deceived they see.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'fantasies' for phantasmata; 'carnal' keeps the bodily, sense-derived character that Augustine contrasts with the pious mind's serenity.

choices.english: by the serenity of a pious mind
choices.why: Keeps the instrumental force of the ablative and the contrast between the mind's calm and the turbulence of carnal fantasies.
rejected: through the clearness of a holy mind

choices.english: the eye of the inner man
choices.why: A literal rendering of the Pauline phrase; 'inner man' is the standard English for interior homo and preserves the biblical echo.
rejected: the eye of the inner self

choices.why: The possessive suum is emphatic: the sun proper to the inner man, not the visible sun. 'Its own' keeps that distinction.
rejected: the sun that belongs to it

choices.why: This is the traditional English rendering of the Latin biblical phrase from Malachi 4:2, and it preserves the genitive of quality.
The diminutive quantulacumque stresses the smallness of the portion; 'however small a part' keeps the concessive force and the modesty of the claim.

bible_refs.note: erat lumen uerum, quod inluminat omnem hominem uenientem in hunc mundum

pass_b_english: Let those rage against you who do not know with what labor truth is found and how difficult it is to avoid errors. Let those rage against you who do not know how rare and arduous it is to overcome carnal fantasies by the serenity of a pious mind. Let those rage against you who do not know with what difficulty the eye of the inner man is healed, so that it can look upon its own sun—not this one you worship in a heavenly body, shining and radiant to the fleshly eyes of both humans and beasts, but that one of which it was said through the prophet: “The sun of justice has risen for me” (Malachi 4:2), and of which it was said in the gospel: “He was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into this world” (John 1:9). Let those rage against you who do not know with what sighs and groans it comes about that God can be understood from however small a part. Finally, let those rage against you who have never been deceived by such an error as the one in which they see you deceived.

last_rejected.quote: not this one you worship in a heavenly body, shining and radiant to the fleshly eyes of both humans and beasts
last_rejected.source_quote: non istum, quem colitis caelesti corpore, oculis carneis et hominum et pecorum fulgentem atque radiantem
last_rejected.why: caelesti corpore modifies the sun's shining, not the place or manner of worship.
last_rejected.fix: not this sun which you worship, shining and radiant with its heavenly body to the fleshly eyes of both humans and beasts
last_rejected.ruling: Ambiguous: 'caelesti corpore' ablative with 'fulgentem atque radiantem' naturally reads as the sun shining in a heavenly body; English 'worship in a heavenly body' misplaces it but is minor-ish... still misleads.
